lessons.title: cognitiō, cognitiōnis — an inquiry, a hearing; knowledge

segments.text: Before the new one: say the Latin for a promise to appear in court, then the Latin for a legal expert.

blocks.title: You'll want to know: cognitiō, cognitiōnis

segments.text: cognitiō, cognitiōnis — "an inquiry, a hearing; knowledge".
Cōnsul cognitiōnem dē caede habuit. The consul held an inquiry into the murder.
cognitiō, cognitiōnis f., built on cognōscō: getting to know, and a judge's hearing of a case. English cognition.
cognitiō is the noun built on cognitus, the participle of cognōscō "to get to know" (EtymDB; Lewis & Short). English cognition comes from it.
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.

lessons.title: quaesītor, quaesītōris — an investigator; a presiding judge

segments.text: Before the new one: say the Latin for a legal expert, then the Latin for an inquiry.

blocks.title: You'll want to know: quaesītor, quaesītōris

segments.text: quaesītor, quaesītōris — "an investigator; a presiding judge".
Quaesītor testēs audīvit. The investigator heard the witnesses.
quaesītor, quaesītōris m., built on quaerō, to seek, to inquire.
quaesītor is built on quaerō "to seek, to inquire" (EtymDB; Lewis & Short), from its participle quaesītus.
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.

lessons.title: interrogō, interrogāre — to question, to examine

segments.text: Before the new one: say the Latin for an inquiry, then the Latin for an investigator.

blocks.title: You'll want to know: interrogō, interrogāre

segments.text: interrogō, interrogāre — "to question, to examine".
Iūdex testem interrogāvit. The judge questioned the witness.
interrogō, interrogāre, interrogāvī, interrogātum, inter + rogō. English interrogate.
interrogō is built from inter "between" and rogō "to ask" (EtymDB; Lewis & Short). English interrogate comes from it.
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.

lessons.title: dēlātor, dēlātōris — an informer, an accuser

segments.text: Before the new one: say the Latin for an investigator, then the Latin for to question.

blocks.title: You'll want to know: dēlātor, dēlātōris

segments.text: dēlātor, dēlātōris — "an informer, an accuser".
Dēlātōrēs multōs innocentēs accūsāvērunt. Informers accused many innocent people.
dēlātor, dēlātōris m., built on the verb for reporting a name to a magistrate. Under the emperors, informers could grow rich.
dēlātor is built on dēlātum, the supine of dēferō "to carry down, to report" (Lewis & Short): one who reports a name. English delator comes from it (EtymDB).
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.

blocks.title: You'll want to know: dēfēnsiō, dēfēnsiōnis

segments.text: dēfēnsiō, dēfēnsiōnis — "a defence".
Dēfēnsiō reī longa fuit. The defence of the accused was long.
dēfēnsiō, dēfēnsiōnis f., the noun of dēfendō. English defence comes through French from the same verb.
dēfēnsiō is the noun built on dēfendō "to ward off, to defend" (Lewis & Short). English defence comes through French from the same verb.
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.

segments.text: A counting board? (abacus, abacī.) A pebble? (calculus, calculī.) To count out? (ēnumerō, ēnumerāre.) To say repeatedly? (dictō, dictāre.) A task? (pēnsum, pēnsī.) Clever? (ingeniōsus, ingeniōsa, ingeniōsum.) Attentive? (attentus, attenta, attentum.) Slow? (tardus, tarda, tardum.) Painstaking? (sēdulus, sēdula, sēdulum.) Careless? (neglegēns, neglegentis.) Knowledge? (scientia, scientiae.) Understanding? (intellegentia, intellegentiae.) Teaching? (doctrīna, doctrīnae.) Ignorance? (īnscītia, īnscītiae.) To imitate? (imitor, imitārī.) A mistake? (mendum, mendī.) A fault? (vitium, vitiī.) A cane? (ferula, ferulae.) A lash? (verber, verberis.) To be beaten? (vāpulō, vāpulāre.) An edict? (ēdictum, ēdictī.) A decree? (dēcrētum, dēcrētī.) A rule? (praeceptum, praeceptī.) Lawful? (lēgitimus, lēgitima, lēgitimum.) Allowed? (licitus, licita, licitum.) A bill? (rogātiō, rogātiōnis.) To publish? (prōmulgō, prōmulgāre.) To repeal? (abrogō, abrogāre.) To make sacred and binding? (sanciō, sancīre.) To lay down? (praescrībō, praescrībere.) The judgement seat? (tribūnal, tribūnālis.) A lawsuit? (līs, lītis.) To go to law? (lītigō, lītigāre.) A promise to appear in court? (vadimōnium, vadimōniī.) A legal expert? (iūriscōnsultus, iūriscōnsultī.) An inquiry? (cognitiō, cognitiōnis.) An investigator? (quaesītor, quaesītōris.) To question? (interrogō, interrogāre.) An informer? (dēlātor, dēlātōris.) A defence? (dēfēnsiō, dēfēnsiōnis.)
